Bernie Sanders
(I-Vt.) seized on former President
Barack Obama
‘s remarks about the Affordable Care Act’s limitations to renew his push for Medicare for All.
Sanders Calls for Medicare for All
On Saturday, Sanders shared a clip of Obama speaking last week at a meeting arranged by House Minority Leader
Hakeem Jeffries
(D-N.Y.), where the former president acknowledged the limitations of the ACA, commonly known as Obamacare.
Sanders wrote on
X
, "President Obama is right: Restoring Obamacare alone is not the answer. There are better systems than the ones we got."
He added, "Every other major country can provide healthcare to all at a far lower cost, yes we can pass Medicare for All and guarantee healthcare as a human right."
Obama Says Obamacare Was Just the Start
Obama described the ACA as a "starter home," saying the law had helped millions of Americans but still left some people falling through the cracks.
"50 million people have used it and benefited from it, but there were still people and there are people now who fall through the cracks because of illnesses," Obama said.
He added that the law was "jerry-rigged on top of a legacy system," saying that was what lawmakers could accomplish at the time.
Obama urged policymakers to pursue further reforms, saying, "There are better systems than the ones we’ve got."
President Obama is right: Restoring Obamacare alone "is not the answer. There are better systems than the ones we got."
If every other major country can provide healthcare to all at a far lower cost, yes we can pass Medicare for All and guarantee healthcare as a human right.
Democrats Push for Health Care Expansion
Sen.
Elizabeth Warren
(D-Mass.) argued that Democrats could reverse Republican health care cuts, expand coverage and fund universal child care without Republican support, urging lawmakers to "get it done."
Democrats can REVERSE Republican cuts to health care, expand health care coverage, and fund universal child care — all without a single Republican vote.
Let’s get it done.
Rep.
Greg Casar
(D-Texas) declared that "health care is a human right," adding that nobody in the wealthiest country should "go broke because they got sick."
Health care is a human right.
Nobody in the richest country on earth should go broke because they got sick.
